title.en: Economics: Gross Domestic Product and its Growth: an Introduction

text.en: Asha asked how we know whether the whole country is growing. "By GDP," said her teacher.

Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is the total value of all final goods and services produced in a country in a year. Gross National Product (GNP) adds income earned from abroad. Net National Product and per capita income are other measures.
GDP is calculated by the expenditure, income and production methods. A rise in GDP means economic growth. Real GDP is adjusted for price changes and nominal GDP is not.
India's economy has three sectors, and services now contribute the most to GDP. Growth should also be inclusive and sustainable, and Tamil Nadu is among the larger state economies.

prompt.en: A friend says GDP counts only farm products. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: It counts all final goods and services.

points.en: GDP = value of final output in a year.
